title: What is known about 1RB0LA_1RC1RA_1RD1RE_1LC---_0RB1LF_1RA0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_1RC1RA_1RD1RE_1LC---_0RB1LF_1RA0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Seen when the head reaches a new cell on the right, the tape is often a list of numbers m written as blocks 1^(4m+2) 0: two more than a multiple of four ones, each followed by a single 0. In the run of 2·1010 steps 57 of the 143 new right cells reached in state D have exactly this form. The numbers range from 0 to about 10 with no evident order, and the last block grows by one 1 at each new right cell (four new cells per visit, in states A, B, C, D). The left end is short and changes little.

The head works in sweeps. Moving right in states A and B (or E, B, C) it turns the alternation 1 0 1 0 1 back into solid blocks; moving left in E and F it turns a solid block into an alternation 1 0 1 0 ..., and A erases runs of 1s. Between sweeps the tape left of the head is a list of blocks 0 1^a of even length (mostly 2 mod 4) and right of the head a list of alternations 1 (0 1)^k separated by gaps 0^(4j+2), with a few irregular cells at the two ends. The halt needs a right-moving A or B to land at the start of a gap of the wrong length: a gap of length 3 in front of A, or 2 in front of B.
verdict: The question is open. The machine halts exactly from C> 0 1 (both directions proved in Lean); the moves before it are fixed, so it halts exactly when, moving right, B meets 0 0 1 or A meets 0 0 0 1 (the runs from these to the halt are proved in Lean; that there is no other way in rests on the table: Lean lists every configuration two steps before a halt, B> 0 0 1 and 0 D> 0, and the second cannot occur because D is entered only from C, which writes a 1 and moves right). Counting every time the head moves right from a 1 onto a 0 over 3·109 steps: A always finds a single 0 or a run of 0s of even length, B a single 0 or a run of odd length (293 million and 145 million times). Halting is a break of this parity law, which nothing has broken; no proof of the law has been found.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 511 cells have been visited and 284 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.116). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.113).

claims.title: The halting context
claims.text: From C> 0 1 the machine reaches its halting transition (proved step by step, then step_none_iff). The halting transition is D reading a 1. D is entered only from C reading a 0 (C writes 1 and moves right); C is also entered from D reading a 0 and moving left, but D comes only from C, so the cell C then reads is the 1 it wrote two steps before, and it moves on to E. The converse is proved: a configuration halts one step later if and only if it is C> 0 1 (halt_iff_1), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_1); halt_pred_2 and halt_pred_3 list every configuration two and three steps before a halt.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: 7 shift rules over the words of the tape (for example (1)^n A> 1 becomes A> 1 (0)^n in n steps and B> (10)^n becomes (11)^n B> in 2n steps), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 20,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the visited tape is 624 cells wide and holds 271 ones.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In the first 109 steps C never had 0 1 under and after it: its contexts are 0 0, 1 0 and 1 1, each about 3.2·107 times. There are no near misses at all at this window, which suggests a local reason (the blocks 1^(4m+2) 0 keep a 0 where C reads a 0).

claims.title: Growth
claims.text: Both ends grow logarithmically: each new cell takes a roughly constant factor more time than the one before.

claims.title: Four more halting contexts
claims.text: Moving right, B on 0 0 1 and A on 0 0 0 1 reach D> 1; B on 1 1 1 after a 0 and F on 0 1 1 after a 0 do too (A erases the two 1s and turns). Each is a fixed run of 2 to 6 steps.

claims.title: The gap-parity law
claims.text: In 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, each time the head moved right from a 1 onto a 0 inside the tape: A found a single 0 290,346,873 times, a run of length 2 mod 4 96,765,873 times and 0 mod 4 1,283 times, never 1 or 3 mod 4 (beyond the single 0); B found a single 0 48,384,348 times, a run of length 1 mod 4 96,764,414 times and 3 mod 4 1,632 times, never an even run. A gap of 3 before A or 2 before B halts. (Runs of 63 or more cells are lumped and not in these counts.)

claims.title: No small finite-automata certificate
claims.text: A finite-automata-reduction search (a DFA of n states on the left part of the tape, the least co-closed NFA on the rest) finds no certificate for any DFA of at most 7 states, with the DFA on the left part or on the right part. A search with closed tape languages whose automata are a hand-written grammar for each side (the blocks and the gaps above, lengths mod 4) times a window of up to 8 cells did not close either: the irregular cells at the two ends of the tape escape the grammar.

claims.title: The shape of the tape
claims.text: Sampled at every 1000th turn of state E on a 0 in the first 3·108 steps, the tape left of the head is a list of blocks 0 1^a with a of length 2 mod 4 or (less often) 0 mod 4, the i-th block often of length exactly 4i (the first 40 kinds of exceptions to 2 mod 4 were all multiples of 4); right of the head a list of alternations 1 (0 1)^k separated by gaps 0^(4j+2), except near the head and at the right end (a lone 1 and a gap of any length).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Is the gap-parity law an invariant? A proof would be a closed language that keeps the gap lengths mod 4 and the arrival state together; it must also cover the two ends of the tape, which do not follow the pattern of the middle.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine has run 20,000,000,000 steps without stopping. Its tape is a list of numbers, each a block of ones two more than a multiple of four. It can stop only from one local pattern, C> 0 1, which it has never produced.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 624 cells visited.
Every halt passes through it, and it always halts (Lean: halt_ctx, halt_iff_1).
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The lengths of the runs of 0s that A and B meet moving right, in 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps; the halt needs the opposite parity.

After 109 steps the tape spans 511 cells (42 left of the start, 430 right), with a density of 1s of 0.556.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The one way to stop
html: The halting transition is D reading a 1. D is entered only from C reading a 0 (C writes 1 and moves right); C is also entered from D reading a 0 and moving left, but D comes only from C, so the cell C then reads is the 1 it wrote two steps before, and it moves on to E. So the machine halts exactly when it produces C> 0 1; Lean proves both directions (halt_ctx: the steps from there to the halt; halt_iff_1: nothing else halts one step later).
How close does it come? What C has ahead of it, counted at every step of the first 109 steps:

sections.heading: What a proof would need
html: Not known. The block form would keep C from ever reading 0 1; what is missing is a proof that the form is kept, or a closed set of configurations that contains the run. Since C has no near misses at all, a tape-language (CTL) proof with a language built on the blocks 1^(4m+2) 0 is a promising route.

The basic moves are proved in Lean for every length (lean/Rules.lean: crossing a run of one word in a fixed number of steps per copy), so a proof would need only the rule of the counter on top of them.

sections.heading: Blocks one way, alternations the other
html: The machine sweeps back and forth over its tape and changes the way the tape is written on each pass. Moving left, states E and F alternate on a block of 1s: E keeps a 1, F writes a 0, so a solid block 1 1 1 1 1 becomes the alternation 1 0 1 0 1. Moving right, A writes a 1 on each 0 and B steps over each 1, so the alternation becomes solid again. Here is one round trip from the run (steps 175 to 190; the head is the letter before >):

175  0 1^2 0 1^4 F> 1^2 0^8 1
180  0 1^2 E> 0^2 1 0 1 0 1 0^8 1          (the block has become 1 0 1 0 1)
190  0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^6 D> 0^5 1          (and solid again, 4 cells longer)
The gap 0^8 in front of the block shrinks by 4 on each such trip: A, B, C and D each fill one of its cells before D turns back. When the gap is used up the block joins the next one.

sections.heading: The parity of the gaps
html: The halt needs a right-moving A or B to land at the start of a gap of the wrong length: A followed by exactly 0 0 0 1, or B followed by exactly 0 0 1 (then C writes a 1 and D reads a 1). Counting every arrival of the head at a run of 0s over 3·109 steps gives a law with no exception:

state arrivingsingle 0length 0 mod 41 mod 42 mod 43 mod 4
A290,346,8731,283096,765,8730
B48,384,348096,764,41401,632

A meets even gaps, B odd ones. Since A and B alternate cell by cell while crossing an alternation, this says the far end of every gap sits at a fixed parity relative to the place where the sweep started. A plausible reason, not checked: the gaps the left sweeps leave behind have length 2 mod 4, a trip on which A arrives fills 4 cells of the gap and one on which B arrives fills 3, and the parity of the arriving state flips accordingly. A proof would have to follow this bookkeeping through the irregular ends of the tape; the automaton searches tried so far (see the ledger) lose track of it there.

summary: Sweeps that turn blocks 1^(4m+2) into alternations 1 0 1 ... separated by gaps 0^(4j+2) and back; halting needs a parity break (A meeting an odd gap or B an even one), never seen in 3·10^9 steps.
